formation.explanation: Leader admits proposals, assigns term/index and emits append requests. Followers match predecessors, protect committed prefixes and defer append support until persistence. Leader tracks qualified replies and selects the active majority or both joint majorities, committing only an advancing current-term entry. It propagates commit through appends and bounded heartbeats; Ready/application consumes the prefix separately. Retry/probe/snapshot paths recover lagging replicas. Configuration application can recalculate commit with different quorum eligibility, but unlike append-reply advancement it does not release queued precommit reads.

context.explanation: Campaigns require promotable membership and scan committed entries after applied for pending configurations. Real campaigns persist votes, aggregate eligible votes and elect an up-to-date leader; pre-vote preserves the term until support is obtained. Higher terms, same-term leader traffic to candidates and quorum loss remove authority; transfer requires caught-up target and times out. Reset clears per-election votes, remote match, read quorum contexts and transfer. Old-term messages cannot contribute ordinary support; committed log prefixes and old snapshot completion survive. Recovery rebuilds term/vote/configuration/log from caller storage.

connection.explanation: Election log freshness and persistent term/vote constrain who may form future decisions; current-term commit and active voter quorums constrain advancement by that leader. Configurations take effect via ApplyConfChange, not at append. Their applied-history bookkeeping is consumed by campaign admission and proposal serialization. Thus application acknowledgement is authority-relevant. Delayed storage messages carry term/context to avoid using obsolete support, while committed decisions and application work are term-independent. Safe reads wait for current-term commitment and quorum context; pending precommit messages differ from the resettable readOnly map.

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe promises linearizable read requests. Node/RawNode ReadIndex promises that the matching read may be processed safely once application advances further than its returned index. For a deterministic register with no intervening later writes, that implies a read invoked after an acknowledged committed write must not return a prior register value when this application condition is met. Demotion is a supported membership operation and StepDownOnRemoval=false is accepted; its role-retention option does not state an exception to safe-read semantics. The check will use actual register application and strict applied>ReadState.Index, not presume index equality sufficient.
grounding.applicability: Caller completes storage and application before Advance, applies a committed simple voter demotion, and keeps the demoted learner in service under its public read API. No clock-dependent lease mode or synthetic reply is needed.

feedback.answered: For the early-Advance Candidate, nextEnts in raft_test.go persists unstable entries, runs delayed messages and advances raftLog.applied but does not apply configuration entries. The campaign test therefore supports the cursor guard but not the legality of deferring an actual configuration callback; NodeAdvance test exercises ordinary entries only. This question remains a scoped contract pause, not explained safety or a defect. Separately, source inspection identifies an independent read-authority discriminator: switchToConfig returns after local removal without changing StateLeader when StepDownOnRemoval is false; stepLeader rejects new proposals when local progress is absent but ReadIndex has no matching eligibility guard. ProgressTracker.IsSingleton tests only the incoming voter count and absence of outgoing voters. Hence its fast path may run for a removed leader when the sole voter is a different node. The next question is whether an API-driven committed removal can leave that node serving a ReadState after the survivor commits a later write. No source read so far requires stopping a removed node, but API applicability and the complete history still need checking.
remaining: Map the emitted ReadState assertion and its authority context; investigate a two-node committed removal through actual RawNode APIs, with StepDownOnRemoval=false and the strict persistence/application-before-Advance order.
Retain the stronger control StepDownOnRemoval=true and normal active singleton read path when constructing a discriminator.
